metadata.notes: Chapter spans several weeks with scene breaks covering survey work, planning changes, and follow-up status checks.

believes: Earth's surviving human population is about fifteen million based on the orbital survey.
The available resources in Sol are enough to build three colony ships and almost enough for a fourth.
Many survivor enclaves will resist relocation or cooperation because of decades of war and xenophobia.
learns: Arthur's global survey identifies nearly forty survivor locations on Earth.
Several survivor groups have shot down drones or destroyed communicators instead of engaging.
Homer's resource survey indicates Sol has enough materials for three colony ships, nearly four.

planets.name: Earth
planets.features: Postwar world with scattered survivor enclaves, some new construction, power generation, and farming operations detectable from orbit.
planets.life: Human survivors remain in nearly forty identified locations.
planets.notes: Riker and Arthur complete a global SUDDAR-assisted survey and estimate about fifteen million survivors.

infrastructure.notes: Riker says the shipyard autofactory should be up and running within two years.

relationships.text: Riker and Butterworth continue their uneasy but functional partnership, negotiating schedule changes and agreeing to shelter additional refugees after the USE group departs.
relationships.notes: The relationship remains tense because Butterworth pushes hard on priorities and timelines.

scenes.summary: Riker convenes a Bob planning session, assigns Charles and Homer to resource scouting and Arthur to Earth-survey work, and reviews colony-ship construction progress.
Riker and Arthur conduct a polar-orbit survey of Earth, identify nearly forty survivor locations, and confront the scale of humanity's collapse.
Riker realizes refugee relocation will require transport vessels and decides to reprioritize manufacturing despite Butterworth's likely objections.
Butterworth challenges Riker over schedule slippage, but agrees refugees can be moved into the USE compound after the main group departs.
Riker checks Arthur's outreach progress and learns many enclaves are hostile or distrustful, while Homer reports enough resources for three colony ships and nearly a fourth.

quotes.speaker: Arthur
quotes.text: Fifteen million people. From twelve billion down to fifteen million. As a species, we’re morons. Maybe we should just let them die and start over.
quotes.context: Arthur reacts bleakly after the Earth survey reveals the scale of humanity's collapse.

threads_opened.text: Arthur's attempts to contact survivor enclaves are meeting distrust and violence, leaving open whether enough groups will cooperate to make a broader evacuation possible.
Riker reprioritizes transport-vessel construction for refugee movement, raising the question of how much this will delay colony-ship production.

threads_resolved.text: Riker and Arthur's completed survey establishes that Earth survived the war in devastated form, with roughly fifteen million humans remaining in scattered enclaves.

events.text: Riker activates two new Sol-based Bobs, Charles and Arthur, to expand resource scouting and Earth-survey operations for the evacuation effort.
Riker and Arthur complete a global survey of Earth, identifying nearly forty survivor enclaves and estimating that only about fifteen million humans remain.

summary.one_line: Riker expands the Sol operation with two new Bobs and confirms that only about fifteen million humans survive on devastated Earth.
summary.paragraph: Riker convenes his local Bob team in Sol and reveals that Butterworth has approved two additional clones, Charles and Arthur, to help with the evacuation effort. He and Arthur then complete a global orbital survey of Earth, locating nearly forty survivor enclaves and estimating that humanity has fallen from twelve billion to roughly fifteen million people. The scale of the disaster forces Riker to rethink logistics, especially the need for transport vessels to move refugees before any colony-ship departures. By chapter's end, Arthur reports that many enclaves are hostile or distrustful of contact, while Homer confirms Sol has enough recoverable resources for three colony ships and almost a fourth.
events: Riker holds a planning session with the Sol Bobs and outlines shipyard, scouting, and Earth-survey assignments.
Riker and Arthur perform a coordinated orbital scan of Earth and identify nearly forty surviving human enclaves.
The survey results show that only about fifteen million humans remain alive on Earth.
Riker realizes that evacuating even a fraction of the survivors will require transport vessels in addition to colony ships.
Butterworth pushes back on schedule changes but agrees refugees can be moved into the USE compound after his people leave.
Arthur reports that many enclaves are refusing contact or attacking drones, while Homer confirms enough resources exist for three colony ships and nearly a fourth.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from managerial confidence into grim recognition of the scale of Earth's collapse, then steadies himself by focusing on practical next steps.

known_planets: Alpha Centauri B inner asteroid belt

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.
One Brazilian vessel escapes the destruction of the Alpha Centauri construction yard, leaving its destination and future threat unresolved.
Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri should be reinforced with combat-class Bobs, raising the question of whether Bill will approve and send them.
Bob has identified an unusually inventive Deltan boy named Archimedes, raising the question of how far his intelligence and toolmaking will develop.
Bob begins activating additional clones at Delta Eridani to support observation and development work, opening the question of how large his local Bob contingent will become.
Arthur's attempts to contact survivor enclaves are meeting distrust and violence, leaving open whether enough groups will cooperate to make a broader evacuation possible.
Riker reprioritizes transport-vessel construction for refugee movement, raising the question of how much this will delay colony-ship production.

recent_events.text: Bob reaches Delta Eridani, starts building up the system, and discovers intelligent alien life on its promising habitable world.
Calvin finds the lost USE probe's wreckage in Alpha Centauri B, then joins Goku in destroying a Brazilian construction yard in Alpha Centauri A.
Riker and Homer move the Sol evacuation plan from negotiation into industrial buildup after confirming enough salvage exists to start construction.
Bob expands his Delta Eridani operation with three new clones and becomes fascinated by an unusually inventive young Deltan he names Archimedes.
Riker expands the Sol operation with two new Bobs and confirms that only about fifteen million humans survive on devastated Earth.
